newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU institutional reform pact near - French minister.
newsitem.headline: EU institutional reform pact near - French minister.

text.p: French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier said on Thursday that an agreement was near on European Union institutional reforms which would help end Europe's status as a "subcontractor for American policy".
"My belief is that today, we are near an overall agreement" on institutional reforms, Barnier told the French daily La Croix.
"However, there are still some points which are causing difficulties, notably on the question of institutions and the makeup of the (European) commission," he said.

EU leaders are to gather in Amsterdam next month in an effort to wrap up the 15-month inter-governmental conference (IGC) which has been mapping out an overhaul of the Maastricht Treaty on European integration.
Ahead of that meeting, EU heads of state and government are to meet on Friday in the Dutch coastal resort of Noordwijk to help prepare for the June 16-17 Amsterdam summit.
Barnier said a successful Amsterdam meeting was crucial to Europe's drive to become "not only a supermarket but a political power".
"We cannot continue to be the subcontractor for American policy," he said.
Barnier also said that the Labour Party victory in Britain had resulted in "a new climate" in the IGC negotiations.
Britain's former Conservative government was deeply sceptical about any drawing closer of the 15-member European Union.
